items.title: Google’s semantic governance policies can block an AI agent’s tool call before it runs
items.snippet: Google lets enterprises put a checkpoint in front of an AI agent‘s actions. Semantic governance policies, in Preview on the Gemini platform, look at each tool call the agent’s model proposes and block it before it runs if the call doesn’t match the user’s request or breaks a company rule. The check sits outside the age
items.summary: Google says its Gemini platform’s semantic governance policies can inspect proposed AI-agent tool calls and block calls that do not match the user’s request.
items.why: Test whether policies block out-of-scope tool calls before they execute.

items.title: Debian 13.8 bundles kernel and Chromium security fixes with a 122-package bugfix list
items.snippet: The Debian project released Debian 13.8, the eighth update to its stable “trixie” series. It mainly carries security fixes, plus corrections for a few serious bugs, and it bundles advisories Debian had already published separately. If you run trixie, here is what to check. The security table runs from DSA-6408 to DSA-6
items.summary: The Debian project says Debian 13.8 includes security fixes, corrections for some serious bugs, and advisories previously published separately.
items.why: If you run trixie, review the update and apply relevant security fixes.

items.title: OpenRouter Drops 3 Providers After Researchers Catch Months of Prompt Theft at AI Hosting Firms
items.snippet: Attackers stole data from inside three AI inference providers for months, and none of the three knew until researchers told them, the industrial cybersecurity company Dragos said this week. Some of the stolen requests were flagged as Zero Data Retention, the setting that is supposed to mean a prompt is never stored. Op
items.summary: Dragos says attackers stole data from inside three AI inference providers for months; the providers learned of the theft from researchers.
items.why: Review data-retention claims and access controls at AI inference providers.

items.title: Researchers Demonstrate Ghostscript Sandbox-Escape RCE via Crafted File Uploads in Popular Apps
items.snippet: A now-patched flaw in Ghostscript allows a crafted file to escape the program's security sandbox and run commands on the server that processes it. Ghostscript is the interpreter that many Linux servers use to convert uploaded PDFs, PostScript files, and images into other formats, often without the application calling i
items.summary: Researchers demonstrated a now-patched Ghostscript flaw that let crafted files escape the sandbox and run commands on servers processing them.
items.why: Check Ghostscript versions and isolate services that process uploaded files.

analysis.headline: Security and maritime activity span systems and seas
paragraphs: The stories describe activity across distinct environments: a reported explosion involving a Russian ship at a Libyan port, attacks on ships in several seas, and claims about tankers in Hormuz. Together, they suggest analysts should track vessel incidents by location while distinguishing reported events from attributed claims.

The cyber items also concern control points: Google’s proposed checks on AI-agent actions and Debian’s bundled security fixes. For defenders, the practical focus is on validating policy behavior and keeping systems current. The GL.iNet report in today’s top stories adds the importance of checking exposed remote-management services.

For analysts, the satellite proposal shows how infrastructure plans can raise both orbital and atmospheric questions. Across the stories, the evidence is uneven: some details are claims, reports, or proposals rather than settled conclusions. Watch for further confirmation and for how these separate developments are described over time.
takeaways: Check AI-agent controls before allowing tool calls to run.
Track maritime reports by location and attribution.
